shoal_e11_entry.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_entry.text: Smoke thinned for a moment, and Yue could see the two support groups waiting beyond the new boundary. Nobody asked her to enter Shed Six. The known workers were out, one badly injured, and qualified care had taken charge of them. The fire captain needed ordinary people for reachable work elsewhere. Yan pointed to the long public route and the short protected relay. 'Choose the task you can stop,' he said. 'Then tell us before you need to stop it.'

shoal_e11_choice_setup_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_choice_setup_01.text: The guide group consisted of four consenting custodians trying to reach a neighboring record annex by the inspected long route. Eight owners' unique annotated tool drawings were stored there, separate from the burning shed's resin stock. Their cabinet could be opened only by its lawful custodians. A qualified fire worker would inspect the annex approach before any receiving. Yue's role would keep the group on the offered safe route and pass current instructions, not become the person entering to seize private papers.

shoal_e11_choice_setup_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_choice_setup_02.text: The short water relay ran behind a qualified protection line. Assigned ordinary helpers would pass small pails at waist height while the fire crew cooled the partition protecting a separate stock bay. That bay held working hardwood compression moulds owned by current tradespeople. The crew would decide entry and later salvage. Yue could handle the approved small pails within her current physical clearance and stop on any altered hand sensation. No cultivation input was part of the task.

shoal_e11_choice_setup_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_choice_setup_03.text: The captain had qualified hands for the fire equipment and current crews for the routes. The support roles overlapped in their urgent opening interval, and available people could not simply crowd both places without blocking work. Yue could accept one. Other helpers were already assigned or had declined after checking their own bodies. Nobody would be punished for staying behind the public boundary. The difference lay in which reachable work gained a willing safe helper now.

shoal_e11_choice_setup_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_choice_setup_04.text: A custodian in the guide group clutched the cabinet key so hard that its teeth marked her palm. She wanted to know whether the drawings were already burning. The captain had no verified answer yet. At the relay, a mould worker asked whether the water would keep every bay intact. The answer was no. Yue heard both hopes meet a qualified limit. She could offer a useful action without promising its material subject would survive.

shoal_e11_choice_setup_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_choice_setup_05.text: Yan told her the relay's small pail held two ordinary liters at its assigned fill mark. The supervised first handling would establish whether it stayed inside her permitted body condition today. A useful circulation did not reduce its physical weight. On the guide route, a shorter smoky passage would remain forbidden even if the custodians insisted. The offered role had to survive pressure from the people whose things it might preserve, not only pressure from flame.

shoal_e11_choice_setup_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_choice_setup_06.text: The record drawings described unpowered tool patterns and owner annotations, not a Lark private freight-signal appendix or Yue's bodily routes. The working moulds carried their own owners and qualified handling limits. Neither group had rights to the other's property. The captain would not use urgency to turn a successful salvage into a public gift. Yue could help carry a message or pail, then leave the actual owners to decide the future of what survived.

shoal_e11_choice_setup_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_choice_setup_07.text: She felt her recent practice failure in her fingertips as a memory rather than a current symptom. The actual check remained her narrow baseline. Her shoulder had not become overhead-safe. She said she could attempt either offered ordinary task and would report a change immediately. Yan nodded and left the selection to her. Being useful did not require proving that a certificate had erased the fear a burning roof put in an ordinary body.

shoal_e11_choice_setup_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_choice_setup_08.text: The guide group's route would take them out of sight of the relay. The relay would keep Yue near its assigned supervisor while the custodians sought another helper or later movement. She would not watch the unchosen role's whole history. Its later material result would need a real report. The fire captain gave each group its current stop and withdrawal signal. Yue listened to both, then chose the work she wanted to do with people who could actually act.

shoal_e11_response_choice.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_response_choice.text: The known workers had been rescued, and qualified crews now faced finite reachable salvage. Yue could guide four consenting custodians along the inspected long route toward eight owners' annotated tool drawings. Or she could join the supervised waist-height water relay protecting a bay of working hardwood moulds. Both roles excluded smoke entry and qi use. Each had a current stop. She chose the ordinary support that would receive her help in this urgent interval.

choices.text: Guide the custodians along the safe long route to the record annex.
Join the small-pail water relay behind the protection line.

shoal_e11_guide_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_01.text: Yue accepted the guide role and repeated its route to the four custodians before moving. One wanted the short passage because she could see the annex roof beyond it. The qualified route hand had closed that passage under current smoke and structural conditions. Yue pointed to the ordinary long-route mark and said they could walk it or remain at the safe waiting place. The woman cursed and chose to walk. Fear had not taken away her right to refuse.

shoal_e11_guide_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_02.text: They moved past the public wall with no one carrying an unassigned heavy load. Yue stayed where the group could hear her ordinary voice without entering an active cart lane. The custodian with the key walked at the back because she wanted to keep everyone in sight. Another nearly ran ahead, then slowed when Yue asked him to stay with the route hand's signal. The group needed its actual people, not the fastest person's imagined shortcut.

shoal_e11_guide_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_03.text: At the first turn, smoke drifted across the planned path. The route hand checked the current condition and held them at the marked ordinary waiting place until the gust cleared. Yue did not use qi to blow a tunnel through it. The custodians watched the seconds pass and accused the wind of choosing sides. She let them speak while keeping the group out of the next cart crossing. Waiting was work when it preserved a usable exit.

shoal_e11_guide_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_04.text: One owner asked whether the drawings had copies elsewhere. Some base patterns did; the unique annotations and one craftsman's hand revisions did not. Losing the cabinet would not erase every trade record in the harbor, but it would lose those particular surfaces and their working evidence. Yue listened to the exact distinction. It gave the role enough importance without turning a cabinet into the last archive holding all the port's lawful existence.

shoal_e11_guide_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_05.text: The route opened after the assigned check. At the annex approach, the qualified fire worker inspected the available entry and named a short receiving interval before withdrawal. The custodians could open their own cabinet; two ordinary authorized helpers would bring sealed bundles to the safe cart. Yue would remain at the receiving boundary and keep the route clear. Her guide role had reached its destination. It had not transformed into an invitation to enter the threatened room.

shoal_e11_guide_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_06.text: The woman with the key tried the wrong tooth first because her hand shook. Nobody snatched it from her. The lawful second custodian steadied the key ring with her permission while she selected the right one. The lock opened. Yue could hear the ordinary click from the boundary and felt an absurd relief that such a small mechanism still worked beneath a burning sky. An artifact with greater power would not have had greater authority to open this cabinet.

shoal_e11_guide_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_07.text: The authorized helpers removed the eight owner-labeled bundles onto the inspected cart. One bundle's outer cord had snagged a shelf corner; they stopped to free it rather than pull through the private annotation inside. The fire worker watched the time and current heat. Yue asked a passerby to keep clear of the receiving lane under the route hand's instruction. The passerby wanted to help and stepped aside when she named the actual job his standing had been blocking.

shoal_e11_guide_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_08.text: The first custodian checked the outer owner marks before any cart moved. All eight identified bundles were present. Their internal condition would need an ordinary later review by the proper owners. The rescue did not permit Yue to unfold them for a dramatic view. She witnessed the exterior count and the actual lawful custody. The woman who had cursed the long path wiped her face and said she had forgotten to breathe normally. Yue told her they could sit once the route was clear.

shoal_e11_guide_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_09.text: The qualified worker closed annex access on the actual withdrawal call. No helper went back for a spare chair or an unoffered private object. The cart moved along the inspected exit while Yue guided the custodians behind it. A gust carried sparks toward a higher roof beyond them, and the fire command redirected its own crew. Yue kept the group within the current route. She could notice another danger without abandoning her assigned people to run toward it.

shoal_e11_guide_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_10.text: At the safe receiving yard, the custodians transferred the sealed bundles under the owners' current storage agreement. The eight drawings had escaped the threatened annex, subject to later actual condition checks. Yue's guide task ended there. The key remained with its lawful custodian, who would keep a later access list. No salvaged private drawing became a public safety poster without its owner's new permission. Surviving material still had a life beyond the helper's good intention.

shoal_e11_guide_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_11.text: From this yard, she could see only the upper edge of the mould bay. Smoke and crew positions hid the water relay's earlier movement. A relay hand later reported that its opening interval had lacked a replacement helper at one critical transfer and the crew had withdrawn from the inner stock approach. Yue did not treat that report as a view she had personally seen. Her choice had supported records, and another reachable material line had lost useful time.

shoal_e11_guide_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_12.text: The mould workers' stock bay burned before qualified salvage could reach its contents. Its working hardwood compression moulds would need an actual later inventory to establish what survived, if anything. Nobody offered Yue a second heroic chance after the roof danger closed that path. The record custodians could be relieved without insisting the other workers' loss was fate. She heard a man cry out at the bay's flame and stayed with the actual receiving instruction.

shoal_e11_guide_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_13.text: A custodian asked Yue to carry one bundle home for safekeeping. Yue declined custody outside the declared owner-controlled storage and asked the lawful keeper to answer the concern. The keeper offered a named locked shelf with the accepted current access process. The custodian chose it. Fear could make familiar hands feel safer than a proper record. Yue wanted to be trusted and still refused a role that would turn her private room into an unauthorized archive.

shoal_e11_guide_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_14.text: When the storage receipt was complete, the four custodians could leave or wait in the safe public area. Two went to find family, one remained beside the keeper, and one sought news of a mould worker she knew. Their shared route ended in different concerns. Yue did not keep them together to complete a grateful group scene. She had guided consenting people through a finite movement. They had no further duty to perform their relief for her.

shoal_e11_guide_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_15.text: Yan found her at the receiving boundary and asked about her current body. The ordinary walking had left her tired but within the reported baseline, with no new tingling. She stopped the assigned task at its completed handoff. He gave her water and told her to stay out of the loading lane while resting. A finished useful role could end before the fire ended. Her ability to keep moving did not create another accepted assignment.

shoal_e11_guide_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_16.text: The tool-drawing owner who had worried about unique annotations arrived at the keeper's shelf. He chose to leave his bundle sealed until daylight and permitted only an exterior count tonight. The drawing's survival would not immediately restart his burned workshop. It preserved a particular working memory he could use later, with new materials and ordinary labor. Yue listened to that smaller future rather than offering a promise that the port would rebuild every loss around it.

shoal_e11_guide_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_17.text: At the public edge, the man whose private tools remained inside Shed Six asked why paper had been saved while his tools might burn. Yue said the annex route had been reachable under the qualified plan and the shed entry had not. She did not rank his livelihood below the drawings. He called the answer useless and turned away. It was a truthful answer to the task and a poor comfort for a person who had just lost control of his next month's work.

shoal_e11_guide_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_18.text: She wanted to follow him with a better sentence. Yan asked her to leave the route clear instead. She obeyed and let the man keep his anger. Sometimes a helper's wish to be forgiven became one more demand placed on a person already paying the loss. The eight bundles remained in lawful storage. The mould bay was burning. She could know the choice had been responsibly made without requiring everyone it failed to help to approve it.

shoal_e11_guide_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_19.text: The qualified fire crew continued containment with actual equipment and current exits. Yue saw a team withdraw from a roof edge that shifted and heard the captain call the changed boundary. Nobody pushed her toward a talisman because the ordinary plan had limits. Her useful quarter-unit task had been a different setup on a different day. Here, the known small action she had completed was guiding people whose keys could open a reachable cabinet.

shoal_e11_guide_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_20.text: A child in the safe waiting area asked if the drawings could show how to put the burned wood back. Its owner said they could show how to make particular tools again from new materials, if the family chose and could fund it. They could not restore old wood. Yue watched the child consider the distinction. Survived knowledge mattered because it offered a possible new task, not because it could reverse the afternoon's actual destruction.

shoal_e11_guide_21.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_21.text: The fire captain marked the annex support completed and the material custody received. He did not pronounce all eight internal drawings sound before owners inspected them. The mould loss remained a different current report. Yue received no wage or cultivation gain for this voluntary role. She had acted within her body and the offered plan, and eight exterior bundles had reached a safe keeper. The exact future usefulness would depend on owners who could still say no.

shoal_e11_guide_22.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_guide_22.text: She sat at last beside the public wall. Her coat smelled of smoke though she had stayed outside it, and her throat felt dry from ordinary shouting. She drank the offered clean water and kept her hands still. The record custodians were no longer a group around her. They had gone to their own concerns. Beyond the boundary, qualified crews were still working, and the unchosen bay's loss would be waiting when she rose.

shoal_e11_relay_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_01.text: Yue accepted the short water relay and repeated its stop instruction to the assigned ordinary supervisor. He gave her the small pail empty first, then filled it to the two-liter mark for a supervised current handling check. She could pass it at waist height with her shoulder inside clearance. No qi entered the water. The pail's usefulness came from the line's position and the qualified fire crew ahead, not from a secret current hiding in her fingers.

shoal_e11_relay_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_02.text: The record custodians sought another offered helper while Yue joined the line. The existing alarm and evacuation assignments could not be abandoned to make one appear. The qualified annex route remained open only during its current safe interval. One custodian wanted to run alone and was stopped at the current boundary. The group had keys and still needed a usable staffed movement. Its unperformed opening chance was a real consequence, not a punishment imposed for preferring moulds to paper.

shoal_e11_relay_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_03.text: The first full pail felt heavier than its amount suggested because Yue's hand expected the familiar practice strip. She adjusted her ordinary grip under the supervisor's instruction and passed it to the next assigned person without twisting. The line had a rhythm like a song stripped of melody. Empty pail, full pail, clear return. She concentrated on the next actual hand instead of the flame beyond the protection line.

shoal_e11_relay_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_04.text: A relay worker stumbled over a moved hose and called stop. The supervisor halted the passing before a filled pail struck him. A qualified hand cleared the current hose position, and the supervisor checked the worker's body before restarting. The delay mattered; the partition's heat did not pause politely. Still, a fallen helper would have narrowed the line and consumed rescue attention. They resumed with the changed obstruction actually removed rather than hoping everyone would remember to step higher.

shoal_e11_relay_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_05.text: At the mould bay, the qualified fire crew used the water inside its actual planned approach. Yue could not see the whole movement behind the partition. She could see the relay continue and hear the crew's current commands. No pail made the wind change or returned consumed resin to a sealed bundle. The purpose was a narrow cooler interval while authorized helpers moved reachable stock through an inspected exit. It was useful because the task was that small.

shoal_e11_relay_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_06.text: After several passes, the familiar fingertip warning returned as a slight altered sensation. Yue told the supervisor at once and set the assigned pail down where he directed. He removed her from handling and called the current ordinary care check rather than praising endurance. The line paused at her position until a willing replacement was assigned by the fire captain. She had helped its opening interval and would not secretly continue to make the earlier choice look wholehearted.

shoal_e11_relay_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_07.text: The qualified ordinary care worker checked her touch and grip in the safe area. He found a current change requiring rest and no more pail passing. The public support-care allowance would pay the accepted assessment under its actual scope; the closed school practice care account was not reopened. He promised no instant repair and retained her overhead restriction. Yue was angry at the timing. Her anger did not give the relay another safe hand.

shoal_e11_relay_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_08.text: The replacement helper accepted the actual pail task after checking its ordinary load and route. The line resumed with the supervisor's current command. Yue stayed behind its boundary and watched empty pails return. Her contribution had not been all-or-nothing. It had bought a useful opening interval, then ended on a body limit. Other people continued the work because they had their own skills and consent, not because her qi remained invisibly sustaining them.

shoal_e11_relay_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_09.text: The qualified team brought the first mould cart through the inspected stock exit. Thirty working hardwood compression moulds were counted under their owners' exterior marks. Four others had visible cracks after heat exposure and were separately retained for qualified later review. The cart's appearance did not prove every saved mould fit for work. Yue saw the outer count from the safe area and heard the fire captain assign the proper receiving, leaving each internal condition for the actual next task.

shoal_e11_relay_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_10.text: The water line helped preserve the partition long enough for that reachable stock movement. It did not keep the whole bay or shed intact. Resin bundles beyond the inspected approach burned, and private tools deeper in Shed Six remained unreachable. A mould worker laughed and cried at once when he saw the marked cart. Yue could let him be relieved without promising that the count had restored his workshop, customers, or lost firing dates.

shoal_e11_relay_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_11.text: At the record annex, the custodians' later movement could not enter once roof danger closed its approach. They stayed outside with their keys as the cabinet's room burned. A current report named the lost opening interval and subsequent unsafe route. Yue had not watched it from her relay position and kept the report separate from personal sight. The eight owners' annotated drawing bundles would need later actual loss confirmation. Nobody could send her back through flame to make the two roles converge into one rescue.

shoal_e11_relay_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_12.text: The custodian who had hoped her key would be enough arrived at the mould receiving yard. She asked why wood had been saved while paper burned. Yue described the current role and qualified approach without ranking the drawings below tools. The woman said she did not want an explanation from the person who had stood in the other line. Yue accepted the refusal. A defensible choice could leave somebody who needed her attention elsewhere and did not want comfort now.

shoal_e11_relay_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_13.text: One mould owner offered Yue an intact small piece as thanks. She declined the gift during emergency receiving because its actual count and condition belonged to the owner's working stock, not an improvised reward table. He could decide later under his own lawful terms, after review. The owner laughed at the premature offer and put it back with its mark. Gratitude could wait until people knew what they actually had left.

shoal_e11_relay_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_14.text: Yan asked whether she had reported the hand change promptly. She said she had and showed the current ordinary restriction. He praised the report, then told her to sit outside the route. The praise did not erase the changed sensation. Her sixth stage remained earned, and her actual support work had ended at its body stop. The line would continue through other willing hands. She did not need to defeat the restriction to remain useful in the crew's account.

shoal_e11_relay_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_15.text: The mould cart's receiving keeper marked thirty apparently working pieces and four visibly cracked ones as provisional exterior states. Proper owners and qualified workers would inspect them later. The keeper retained the actual location and custody. No salvaged piece became a public pattern simply because ordinary people had passed water nearby. The old deceased maker's lost printing blocks were unrelated to these different workers' compression tools, and none of his original cut surfaces had magically returned in the cart.

shoal_e11_relay_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_16.text: At the public edge, the man whose private tools remained inside asked Yue whether the mould cart held his. It did not. The qualified route had reached a different stock bay, and his shed location remained unsafe. He drank the offered water and cursed the answer. Yue could not make every tool owner included by calling the cart generally salvaged property. His possible loss stayed with its own actual location, owner, and later inventory.

shoal_e11_relay_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_17.text: The fire captain closed the first stock movement once the partition route changed. No helper stayed inside because a fourth cracked mould seemed repairable. The team had preserved what the current safe interval allowed and withdrawn under its actual command. Yue watched them cross into the cooler public area, tired and sweating. They were ordinary qualified workers who could still be frightened by a roof shifting above them. Expertise had given them exits, not immunity.

shoal_e11_relay_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_18.text: A child beside the mould cart asked if the drawings in the annex were needed to use the pieces. The owner said some tools could be used from retained ordinary practice, while unique annotations and repairs in the burned bundles could be lost. Surviving wood did not replace every knowledge surface. New drawings might be made by skilled people later and would be new records. Yue liked the owner's refusal to turn a saved cart into a promise that nothing important remained missing.

shoal_e11_relay_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_19.text: The care worker checked Yue's current hand again before allowing her to leave the safe rest area. She remained off load handling for the rest of the emergency interval and would attend a dated next-day review. She could walk the licensed public route with rest, without joining a new relay under another name. The fire captain did not ask her to circumvent the restriction by carrying smaller pails forever. A stop needed to end actual work, not merely change its label.

shoal_e11_relay_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_20.text: She sat with the changed fingers resting on her own coat. The ordinary ache made the earlier successful marker task feel distant but not false. It had qualified a different load and condition after recovery. Today's repeated physical pails had reached a new limit, and she had stopped. She could remember both results without deciding that one invalidated the other. The known useful work remained modest enough to describe exactly: part of a relay's first safe interval.

shoal_e11_relay_21.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_21.text: The record custodians left in different directions after the annex approach closed. One went to find a business partner, one stayed with the keeper's loss report, and two walked together without wanting company. Yue did not follow them to solicit forgiveness. Thirty provisionally working moulds and four damaged pieces stood in a guarded cart. The eight drawing bundles remained inaccessible in a burning room. The line had moved material, and its opposite loss would continue in other people's lives.

shoal_e11_relay_22.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_relay_22.text: The fire command marked the relay support's actual interval and the stock custody received. No wage or cultivation gain attached to Yue's voluntary role. The emergency-care assessment belonged to its own accepted source, with her restriction still active. She had changed what a crew could preserve without becoming the source of its water, courage, or skill. Beyond the boundary, the larger shed still burned, and the next task would be to contain what their finite people could contain.

shoal_e11_after_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_after_01.text: By late afternoon, the qualified fire crew had stopped trying to preserve the whole of Shed Six. Its command focused on preventing spread into occupied neighboring rooms and keeping the exits usable. Some stock burned beyond safe entry. The captain said the loss plainly so property owners would not mistake a withdrawn crew for a new secret salvage plan. Yue sat behind the public boundary, carrying the particular support role she had completed and the larger work she had not.

shoal_e11_after_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_after_02.text: The known rescued workers reached qualified ordinary care under the local emergency receiving process. Their employer's held Shed Six care deposit offered one hundred twenty copper for care, supplies, travel, and finite restricted-income support, subject to accepted plans. It did not buy complete recovery or every later lost commission. Each worker retained consent over care and public information. The injured partner who had gone with the fourth worker would hear his plan from the clinician, not from a rumor at the fire rope.

shoal_e11_after_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_after_03.text: The public support helpers had a separate twelve-copper ordinary-care allowance for two six-copper assessment and follow-up slots. A strained-wrist helper attended one after reporting his symptoms. The other would pay a second appropriate assessment if used, or return unused to its source. No closed school or restoration reserve was reopened. Emergency work had current funding responsibilities as well as shouted instructions, and a volunteer's body did not become free material simply because her task was unpaid.

shoal_e11_after_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_after_04.text: The fire captain asked for people counts again when the crowd moved. A family that had left the public waiting space was confirmed safe by its offered message through the contact. Another arrived looking for a worker whose ordinary shift had ended elsewhere. The clerk checked the appropriate roster. Nobody treated every absence as a missing person inside the shed. Panic made such mistakes understandable, and the staffed count made them less likely to send a crew into needless danger.

shoal_e11_after_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_after_05.text: A woman wanted to keep the gate open for her husband even after the waiting space shifted. The attendant showed her the new location and contact rather than leaving an unsafe old gate as a symbol of hope. She moved reluctantly and asked the same question there. Yue could see how a marked route might feel cruel when somebody needed it to remain familiar. The answer did not require the woman to stop being afraid.

shoal_e11_after_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_after_06.text: At the clinic route, the messenger returned with permitted updates on receiving, leaving private treatment detail with the workers and clinicians. All four known employees had reached care. The fourth's leg injury needed a longer qualified plan. Current receiving did not establish a outcome. Yue drank water slowly and listened to the messenger give that limit to a man asking whether rescue meant everyone was now fine.

shoal_e11_after_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_after_07.text: Rong's supplier cart stayed outside the fire area under its owner's instruction. It did not carry a talisman that could cool a roof. The merchant spoke with the fire captain about actual charcoal stored elsewhere and the current separation from flame. He had a legitimate interest in preserving his goods and a duty not to obstruct rescue. He accepted the route's closure even while asking when his next delivery could lawfully move.

shoal_e11_after_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_after_08.text: He Ming helped packing workers account for their own people and goods outside the affected sheds. His group had no authority to open a private cabinet or assign the fire crew. He could carry offered locations to the responsible command. A worker who had refused the earlier room move still supplied a useful count. Disagreeing with one plan had not excluded her from the town's safety work or made her less deserving of help.

shoal_e11_after_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_after_09.text: Song Mei was at a different licensed room when the alarm began. She heard the public notice and ended her offered rehearsal safely under its keeper's instructions. She would not be counted among the shed's eyewitnesses because she arrived later. When she reached Yue's waiting area, she asked about her present condition and listened to the actual answer. The performer offered company for a short while without turning her friend's fear into a piece for tomorrow's audience.

shoal_e11_after_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e11_after_10.text: They sat on the public wall's cooler side. Song Mei said the room keeper had wanted to continue rehearsal because the paid hour was already running. She had refused and accepted the lost remainder. Yue thought of her own bounded emergency role and how hard it had been to end. The artist's choice had protected people in a different room. No flames had reached that room, and its safety would not need a fabricated near escape to count.
